nodes.name: Source documents
nodes.detail: Collect approved documents with stable document IDs, version metadata, and access permissions. This demonstration uses an invented employee handbook.

nodes.name: Parse & chunk
nodes.detail: Extract text and split it into useful passages. Attach document ID, section, chunk ID, version, and permissions so evidence can be traced later.

nodes.name: Embed passages
nodes.detail: Encode each passage using the embedding model used by query retrieval. Store vectors alongside the original text and provenance.

nodes.name: Knowledge index
nodes.detail: Index passage vectors and text with provenance and access metadata. Retrieval uses the same embedding space; permission filters limit which chunks can be returned.

nodes.name: User question
nodes.detail: Receive the question and access context. The example asks how many annual leave days can be carried over.

nodes.name: Retrieve candidates
nodes.detail: Embed the question, search the knowledge index, and return candidate passages with their source references. Retry uses a rewritten question. Empty or unusable results go to the evidence gate.

nodes.name: Rerank evidence
nodes.detail: Score candidate passages against the question, remove irrelevant evidence, and order the strongest matches. If all candidates are rejected, send the result to the evidence gate.

nodes.name: Assemble context
nodes.detail: Build the model input from selected passages and their source IDs. Keep the question and instructions separate from retrieved content, and stay within the context budget.

nodes.name: Evidence gate
nodes.detail: Handle an empty search or a reranker that rejects every passage. Allow one query rewrite. If the second attempt still has no usable evidence, abstain instead of generating an unsupported answer.

nodes.name: Rewrite & retry
nodes.detail: Clarify or expand the search wording without changing the user intent or access scope. Retry retrieval once. The simulation then shows recovered evidence; the exhausted branch remains visible.

nodes.name: Generate answer
nodes.detail: Generate an answer grounded in the retrieved passages and attach source markers to supported claims. Relevant retrieval improves grounding but does not guarantee that every generated claim is correct.

nodes.name: Resolve citations
nodes.detail: Map generated source markers to real retrieved chunk IDs and source locations. Check that IDs exist and the referenced passages support the claims. Drop or flag unsupported claims; reference validity alone is not proof of support.

nodes.name: Abstain safely
nodes.sub: Ask for a source or clarification
nodes.detail: When the retry budget is exhausted, explain that the available documents do not contain enough evidence. Ask for a document or a clearer question; do not invent a supported answer.

nodes.name: Grounded response
nodes.detail: Show the answer with inspectable citations. Example: “You may carry over up to five days [1].” The source is the illustrative employee handbook, section 4.2, chunk-017.

steps.text: Extract text, then preserve document IDs while splitting passages.
Encode each passage into a vector. Keep the original text and source reference.
Store vectors, passage text, permissions, and provenance in the knowledge index.
Start with the question: “Can I carry over annual leave?”
Search the index using the question embedding and access filters.
Return candidate passages with their source references.
Rerank the candidates and retain evidence relevant to carryover limits.
Assemble the strongest passages into the generation context.
Generate a draft with source markers for supported claims.
Resolve citations: up to five days [1], linked to handbook §4.2.
The initial question enters retrieval.
The initial search finds no usable passage.
No evidence: route to the evidence gate before generating an answer.
One rewrite is allowed: “annual leave carryover policy maximum days.”
Retry retrieval once with the clearer wording and the same access filters.
Search the index again. In this simulated branch, a useful passage is found.
Recovered: the handbook carryover passage is returned.
Rerank the recovered evidence and keep the strongest passage.
Build a context containing the recovered passage and its source ID.
Generate only after usable evidence is available.
Recovered answer: up to five days [1].
Alternative: if retry also finds no evidence, abstain and request clarification.

title: From knowledge to grounded answers.
subtitle: Follow the evidence. See what happens when retrieval fails.

footer.text: “Employees may carry over up to five days of annual leave.” [1]
footer.note: Document IDs and chunk references stay attached through retrieval, reranking, and generation.
